I'm designing a motion/"juice" system (animations, shader accents, interaction variants) for Twyne, a Qwik + Convex local-first writing app at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne. Brand: editorial, letterpress, literary writer's room (paper, ink, stamps, vermilion/cobalt). I need a precise inventory of the **Desk** page so I can give every component a purposeful interaction. Do not edit anything.

Scope: `src/routes/desk/index.tsx` and everything it renders from `src/components/desk/*` (recent-work, writing-activity, daily-activity-chart, chart-table, usage-cost, hosted-cost, usage-breakdowns, token-dimensions, writer-patterns, desk-summary, data-controls, public-desk, usage-sync-controller). Also the loading state ("Reading the ledger") and empty states. Find the global.css rules for the classes these components use (src/global.css is 10k lines — grep for the class names, don't read it whole).

For EACH visible component/sub-element report, compactly:
1. file:line of its root JSX, and what it shows.
2. Every user interaction it supports (hover, click, keyboard, scroll, drag, toggle, link) and what that interaction does.
3. Current feedback/motion: existing transitions, keyframes, hover styles, focus styles, loading/empty/error variants (cite class names + the global.css line numbers).
4. The *consequence class* of each action: local-only (stays on device), syncs to account, sends data to an AI provider / costs hosted credits, publishes publicly, destructive/irreversible, or navigation only.
5. Data it displays that changes over time (counts, charts, costs) — i.e. what could animate on arrival or update.
6. Anything inconsistent with other Desk components (different card styles, radii, shadows, header styles).

Also list: the CSS custom properties for colour/typography/z-index used (e.g. --color-paper, --color-ink, --color-vermilion, --color-cobalt, --font-display, --font-serif), and any existing motion tokens/easing curves or reduced-motion handling that the desk uses.

Return a structured list (one block per component), terse, with file:line references. No prose essays. Under ~1200 words.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
